operations.description: This commits real money and lab work. Confirm with the user first. Use `validateAssay` beforehand.

No order is created and nothing is charged, but the lab is sent your sequences, and A-Alpha keeps a quote on file. The order gets the same checks as `validateAssay` first: one that fails them is 422 `validation_failed` with the same problems in `errors`, and nothing reaches the lab. No Assay Portal access is 403 `wetlab_access_required`; an unclaimed agent trial credential is 403 `forbidden`. When Ginkgo gives no price, its catalog price is used.

200 means the check ran, whatever the verdict. Only a body with no `assayType`, a field of the wrong JSON type, an unknown field, or text that isn't valid Unicode is 422, because there is nothing to check. The body is `AssayOrderCheckRequest`: every other rule of `AssayOrderRequest` (exactly one of `sequences` or `csvFile`, `modality`, the shape of each sequence) is part of the verdict. Runs the portal's own order checks, word for word: settings, sequences, a CSV file (read from your own files only), targets, residues, each lab's minimums and duplicates. Nothing is created and no lab is conta…
Your own order. Another account's order, a portal draft, a deleted order and an unknown id are all 404.

Confirm with the user first. The order's `cancellable` field says whether this will work now. Safe to repeat: an order already `cancelled` or `cancelling` answers 200 as it is. When the lab holds the order it is told: Ginkgo confirms later, so the order reads `cancelling`; A-Alpha confirms at once. An order no lab holds yet is only recorded as `cancelled`. Ginkgo orders can be cancelled only before work starts, A-Alpha orders until they finish, and Adaptyv and GenScript orders only through Tamarind support.

Links to what the lab delivered; `expiresAt` says when they stop working. Results stored with Tamarind are listed whatever the order's `status` says now; otherwise nothing is ready until the order is `completed`. A completed order with nothing stored yet asks the lab once more: GenScript's report or Adaptyv's results are fetched, stored and recorded on the order. Ginkgo and A-Alpha deliver on their own, so there is nothing to ask. An Adaptyv order's own data-package links are fetched again on each read, waiting at most 5 seconds.
